acquisition method: We analysed the Plasmodium falciparum schizont phosphoproteome using for the first time, a data-dependent neutral loss-triggered-ETD (DDNL) strategy and a conventional decision-tree method.
alkylation reagent: cysteine alkylation was performed in situ with iodoacetamide
cleavage agent: proteins were digested with Trypsin Gold (Promega)
enrichment method: Two acquisition strategies were employed to identify phosphopeptides from IMAC enriched P. falciparum phosphopeptide samples.
fragmentation method: the combination of Mascot Percolator and turbo-SLoMo represents a robust workflow for phosphoproteomic data analysis using CID and ETD fragmentation.
instrument: coupled to an LTQ Orbitrap Velos hybrid mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific)
ionization type: equipped with a nanospray ion source.
labeling: We also performed proteome profiling experiments (1 μg of desalted FASP digest) using direct LC–MS/MS analyses
reduction reagent: Parasite pellets were re-suspended in extraction buffer (4% SDS, 0.1 M DTT, 0.1 M Tris pH 8, 0.5 mM PMSF, 2 μg/ml Aprotinin/Leupeptin, 20 μM ZnCl and 25 mM Sodium fluoride)
reduction concentration: Parasite pellets were re-suspended in extraction buffer (4% SDS, 0.1 M DTT, 0.1 M Tris pH 8, 0.5 mM PMSF, 2 μg/ml Aprotinin/Leupeptin, 20 μM ZnCl and 25 mM Sodium fluoride)
